overall: The AG found the Wareham Finance Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by voting by secret ballot and by posting an insufficiently specific notice for its September 8 meeting; the secret ballot violation was cured by a properly noticed revote on September 15. Members must complete training.

allegations.summary: Committee voted by secret ballot (Australian ballot) to recommend a new member at its September 8 meeting; the complainant objected at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee violated the Law when it voted by secret ballot at its September 8 meeting.

allegations.summary: September 8 notice listed only 'Vote for Chair position,' but the Committee also voted for vice chair and clerk; complaint alleged the notice was insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: Because notice of the September 8 meeting did not include appointment of a vice chair and clerk as a topic, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law when it discussed and voted on those appointments at the September 8 meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
All Committee members must attend an Open Meeting Law training webinar provided by the AG's office within 90 days of the letter and certify that they have done so.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
